shorts.description: “I’ve been getting copies by my competition, how would you react?”
shorts.title: A Billion Dollar Company Just Copied My Product

shorts.description:
Before saying you have ADD: put your phone in another room, turn off notifications, plug your ears, make a list, then work on the list.

You focus by removing everything but the work, not adding things.

Give yourself a chance before you say you have a disorder.
shorts.title: How to Stay Focused

shorts.description:
I am the biggest success story of every mentor/coach/vendor I’ve ever paid.

Here’s my “secret”:
Do everything they tell you to. 
To the tee. 
The first time. 
Take what works. 
Toss the rest.

You can learn something from everyone.
But only take in that which makes you stronger.
shorts.title: I Joined a Gym Mastermind Before I Owned a Gym

shorts.description:
A lot of entrepreneurship comes down to being able to look an existential threat in the eyes with equal parts dread and enthusiasm. 

And going from “this is gonna end us” to “we can turn this into a win” as fast as possible.
shorts.title: Choose Between Some Jobs Lost or All Jobs Lost

shorts.description:
If the words money and power bother you, you’ll never get them.

They’re neither good or bad.

They can build hospitals or fund terrorism.

But if you want to do big shit, you’re gonna need a lot of both.
shorts.title: Money and Power Can Save Countries. Peace Can Only Save Me.

shorts.description:
Who you sell to matters as much (or more than) the value you provide:

If you help a billionaire lose weight you can charge 100x more than gen pop. 

Because in a very real way, that more narrowly defined market values the solution at a higher dollar amount.
shorts.title: Same Sales Velocity, But LTV Is 5-10x Higher

shorts.description:
We’re all addicted to the same thing: reward. 

The only difference is what we get it from and where it leads us.
shorts.title: Give Someone a Label and They'll Change Their Own Behavior

shorts.description:
How to beat a bigger competitor: 
Talk to customers more than they do.

He who is closest to the customer wins.
shorts.title: You're Not Competing Against the Company, You're Competing Against Rep #7

shorts.description:
As silly as this sounds - almost no one does it:

If you’re trying to achieve something, the first step is having a way to measure progress.

And the more ways you measure, the more ways you can win.

So start there, then don’t stop winning.
shorts.title: How to Measure Customer Happiness

You focus by removing everything but the work, not adding things.

Give yourself a chance before you say you have a disorder.
shorts.title: You Don't Have to Write, But You Can't Do Anything Else

shorts.description:
Download your free scaling roadmap here: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap-yt-d

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

shorts.title: 8 Entrepreneurs Compete For $100,000Scale or Fail Season 1. Premiering this Friday, June 26th

shorts.description:
Trying to be happy is what makes you sad.

You don’t get over sadness by striving for the opposite, but by ceasing to label your emotional state as good or bad in either direction.

#fvckhappiness became my mantra and released me my self judgment. 

I am. That is enough.
shorts.title: Stop Chasing Happiness, Start Chasing Things You Can Do

shorts.description:
If I could tell my 22-year-old self one thing about sales: Stop trying to convince people who can't afford it. A broke person who says yes is worse than a rich person who says no.

If you want to get money, go where the money is.
shorts.title: You're Ashamed of Not Having Integrity With Your Own Pricing

shorts.description:
As silly as this sounds - almost no one does it:

If you’re trying to achieve something, the first step is having a way to measure progress.

And the more ways you measure, the more ways you can win.

So start there, then don’t stop winning.
shorts.title: How to Measure Customer Happiness (Paired Metrics)

shorts.description:
If you have no money, you should have no shame.

Knock.
Call.
Email.
Text. 
DM.
Ask. 

Life-changing doors don’t open themselves.
shorts.title: If You Have No Money, You Should Have No Shame

shorts.description:
You don't need a reason to raise your prices.

Wanting to is reason enough.
shorts.title: How to Raise Your Prices Without Losing Clients

shorts.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.
shorts.title: Why Every New Opportunity Is the Woman in the Red Dress

shorts.description:
Regular people will never understand just how many times champions practice in private before they perform in public.

Once they do, they stop being regular people and become champions too.
shorts.title: Winners Are Relieved, Losers Are Excited

shorts.description:
One of the hardest parts about business is the worry that all the work, money, and time you’re investing right now, and have invested, will amount to nothing.

And - you just gotta deal with it, get back to work, and try and prove it wasn’t.
shorts.title: You Bought a Business, Not a Passive Investment

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can’t help themselves…

When business growth slows, they think ‘What’s something new I can sell my audience?’

Rather than, ‘How I do the hard thing and keep growing my main thing?’

New doesn’t compound.

Better questions better answers.
shorts.title: You Could Also Just Do More of This Thing

shorts.description:
If you’re trying to start a business:

Just. Find. Shit. People. Already. Buy. And. Sell. It.

You can figure out passion purpose etc after you learn the basics. 

Make a profit. Then get cute.

But you may realize you find you’re passionate about making a profit.

2 birds.
shorts.title: You Don't Need an Original Idea

shorts.description: You only need to get rich once. So you might as well work as hard as you can to get it done as fast as you can.
shorts.title: I Lost Everything Twice Before Hitting $100M at 31

shorts.description:
Sometimes it really is as simple as:

Double your leads. 
Double your business.
shorts.title: You Don't Have a Conversion Problem, You Need More Ads

shorts.description: You'll be rewarded far more in life for your determination than your intelligence. The problem is - determination just looks like a long string of failures until it works.
shorts.title: You're Rewarded for Enduring Failure, Not Avoiding It

shorts.description:
The reason why some people won’t buy your services, even if you give them away, is because the price isn’t the only cost to the prospect.

If you can identify all the other costs, and remove them, you’ll learn how to sell more when you do start charging full price.
shorts.title: Stop Calling Your Business Commoditized

shorts.description:
Common Q: “How would you start a business with $1000?” 

My .02: 

1) Put the money in your pocket and ignore it.

2) Pick if you’re gonna sell other people stuff, or stuff you can finance thru prepayment, or use OPM to finance it.

Money isn’t the limiting factor, knowledge is.
shorts.title: Never Give Away Equity for $1,000

shorts.description:
Most people never start making money because they can’t even admit that they suck. 

They stay stuck in the delusion that they somehow have an amazing product that no one wants and no one talks about.

If you were the best, you’d be making money.

So. You’re not. Now work.
shorts.title: Go Live Every Day for 2-3 Hours (No One Knows You Suck Yet)

shorts.description:
You can’t become anyone new if you’re unwilling to give up who you were.

You can’t get anywhere new until you leave where you are.

We always have to risk what we have for what we want.
shorts.title: Every Good Thing in Life Has a Dark Side

shorts.description:
Simplest path to making money:

1) Find a service people already buy
2) Do it in half the time, make it twice as easy for the customer, or remove all risk
3) Ask everyone you know if they know anybody who wants it
4) Charge more than everyone else
5) Dont stop when u get bored
shorts.title: Why Your Side Hustle Never Became a Business

shorts.description:
If you’re having trouble making a profit in your business consider:
1) Selling to richer customers
2) Raising your prices
2a) Delivering faster
2b) Offering a guarantee
2c) Making things even easier for your customer 

Im talking 2-10x price increases. Not 10-20%. Move the needle
shorts.title: More Demand Than You Can Handle? Raise Your Price

shorts.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.
shorts.title: 40 Stores vs 330 Stores: Which Gets You to $100M?

shorts.description:
I recommend spending all excess cash on acquiring skills until you have so much that you can't possibly spend it on more skills.

Increase your capacity to earn, which increases the value of your highest cash-producing asset (you).

Relevant for today - skills are inflation-proof
shorts.title: Skills Can't Be Taxed, Seized, or Taken in a Divorce

shorts.description:
My favorite business building question:

“What’s the one thing, that if I stopped doing today, would immediately destroy my business?”

Now, instead of stopping, do ten times more of it.
shorts.title: If You Can Get to $100M Selling One Thing, Why Would You Sell Three?

shorts.description:
When I started out, I used to guard my "IP" with my life. I thought "these are my secrets, I suffered so much to learn them - I dont want anyone to know"

I literally used to lie at masterminds about how much money we made (under-reported) so no one would ask me what I was doing. 

Then I could just take notes on everyone else. 

What a mistake. So silly.

One of the coolest things in my life is seeing the stuff I write and make content about being used in new ways to make money everyday by #Mozination. 

Many started from scratch using YT content + my book and create wildly profitable businesses. 

Everyday we get about 10 businesses doing over $3,000,000 per year who apply to become portfolio companies.

The innovation of the community (and our portfolio CEOs) teaches me more than I ever learned on my own. 

It's like getting 1000 lifetimes of innovation all at once on your favorite subject - makin money. 

We're all here because other humans figured stuff our and passed it on. We're all gonna die. And if your knowledge dies with you, it's a waste of a life. 

Education is the greatest legacy of all.
shorts.title: Patents Mean Nothing Until Your Business Makes Money

shorts.description:
I was talking to a friend of mine who decided recently to get into the content game.

He asked why my content was getting more reach than his.

I said “I don’t know. We put out about 250 per week. How many pieces a week are you putting out?”

He replied “I’m posting a measly once a day. Ha! Thank you for resetting my minimum standard.”

He’s already an incredibly successful man (more than me) and it instantly clicked for him. 

Volume. (But there’s more to it than that)

I’ve had this happen to me in business more times than I can count.

I think “oh I should just do 30% more or 50% more.”

But the people who are beating me aren’t doing 50 PERCENT more, they’re doing 50 TIMES more. Big. Difference.

We think we’re doing something wrong, but in reality we aren’t doing nearly enough of it.

To get 5x the results sometimes you have to put in 50x the effort.
shorts.title: How to Know If It's Not Working or Just Not Seen Yet

shorts.description:
You either grow into your potential or you keep living the same six months over and over again. 

The difference is how many hard conversations you’re willing to have and how fast you have them once you realize you need to.
shorts.title: Everything You Want Is on the Other Side of Hard Conversations

shorts.description:
When you nail your offer, it’s an order of magnitude change in a business. 

You can 2x, 10x, even 100x a business with a better offer. 

Sales - although a valuable skill - can only improve a business incrementally.

This is why we focus on the offer before anything else.
shorts.title: Why High LTV Doesn't Have to Mean High CAC

shorts.description:
You can work to get anything you want. But you have to sacrifice other things you want to keep it.

And that’s sometimes harder than the work.
shorts.title: If You Want Everything From Life, You'll Get Nothing

shorts.description:
You’re going to die.

And a few months later, no one will think about the risks you took or didn’t take.

What a waste to live your entire life to please people who will never think of you again. (Or ever to begin with)
shorts.title: Most People In Your Life Won't Be Here Forever

shorts.description:
There comes a time in every business owners life where he switches from how much money can I make to how little can I do to make it?

I’ve often found I can accomplish both by asking the second question first. 

Then, scaling zero time in.
shorts.title: Drop the 1-on-1s and Triple Your Revenue

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can dramatically increase their net worth by doing less.

If you can hire the people to run your business without you, truly, as in, someone else could buy the bank account and it would continue to get deposits…you have a valuable thing. 

Worth prioritizing.
shorts.title: You Don't Have to Sacrifice Your Family for Your Goals

shorts.description:
Progress over pride

No one remembers if you asked for help.
shorts.title: No One Remembers If You Asked for Help. They Remember If You Won.

shorts.description: You don't need a product to start. You need attention.
shorts.title: You Don't Need a Product to Start, You Need Attention

shorts.description:
How to build an amazing brand in a nutshell:

1) Figure out what everyone else charges for
2) Make it better
3) Make it free

(…and monetize another way)
shorts.title: Your Price Is Too Low and It's Hurting You

shorts.description:
I recommend spending all excess cash on acquiring skills until you have so much that you can't possibly spend it on more skills.

Increase your capacity to earn, which increases the value of your highest cash-producing asset (you).

Relevant for today - skills are inflation-proof
shorts.title: Skills Can't Be Taxed, Seized, or Taken in a Divorce
